questions.q: Why isn't vector similarity a perfect proxy for relevance?
options: Vector similarity is computed from each chunk and the query independently, so two chunks can score similarly close while only one actually answers the question
Vector similarity always returns results in a random order
Vector databases do not return a numeric similarity score
Vector similarity only works for chunks under 100 tokens
questions.explain: Because chunk embeddings and the query embedding are each computed independently, similarity is a good but imperfect approximation of true relevance.

questions.q: What does a re-ranker (cross-encoder) do differently from vector search?
options: It stores pre-computed embeddings for faster lookup
It takes the query and a candidate chunk together as one input and scores that specific pairing's relevance
It replaces the embedding model entirely
It only works with image data
questions.explain: A re-ranker jointly evaluates the query and chunk together, which is more accurate than comparing two independently-computed vectors — but too expensive to pre-compute and store.

questions.q: In the Cohere Rerank API example, what does the 'documents' field contain?
options: Every chunk in the entire vector database collection
The candidate list that vector search already narrowed down, typically the top 20-50 chunks
A list of user accounts with rerank permissions
The final answer text to return to the user
questions.explain: Re-ranking runs on the already-narrowed candidate list from vector search, not the full collection, because the joint query-document scoring is too expensive to run on millions of chunks.

questions.q: In a Rerank API response like { "index": 1, "relevance_score": 0.97 }, what does 'index' refer to?
options: The chunk's position in the vector database's internal index structure
A random ranking identifier with no connection to the request
The position of that document within the original 'documents' array sent in the request
The page number of the source document
questions.explain: index refers back to the position in the request's documents array, so the caller can match each relevance score to the original chunk it scored.

questions.q: Why does re-ranking run after vector search instead of replacing it?
options: Re-ranking cannot process more than one document at a time
Vector search is required by law for all RAG pipelines
Re-ranking would produce identical results to vector search
Running the more expensive, query-aware re-ranker against an entire collection instead of a narrowed candidate list would be too costly and slow at real scale
questions.explain: Vector search cheaply narrows a huge collection to a short candidate list; the re-ranker then spends its more expensive, more accurate judgment only on that short list.
